name: /plan
description: Ground a plan in your files, name the key decisions, save it to .agents/plans/, and stop for approval before any code changes.

examples.command: /plan Add a transfer operation with overdraft protection
examples.explanation: Produce a decision-complete plan and stop for approval.

when_to_use: The work has decisions to make before code: an API to design, a migration to sequence, a PR to split.
when_not_to_use: It is explicit-invocation only; task complexity alone does not trigger it, and it does not plan ordinary implement, fix, or refactor requests.
notes: The extending page lists this bundled playbook as /plan, matching the cookbook.

name: /grilling
description: Interview you one decision-forcing question at a time until the design is sharp.

examples.command: /grilling Pressure-test the transfer and overdraft design
examples.explanation: Have the agent play skeptic one question at a time.

when_to_use: You have a rough idea and want its assumptions pressure-tested before you build.
when_not_to_use: It is explicit-invocation only; Muse Code does not run it because a request looks underspecified.
notes: The extending page calls this playbook /grill while the cookbook documents it as /grilling. Run /help to see the name your build exposes.

name: /grill-with-docs
description: Run the same decision-forcing interview and write the settled decisions into your project docs.

examples.command: /grill-with-docs Pressure-test the transfer design and record decisions
examples.explanation: Turn interview answers into durable project knowledge.

when_to_use: The interview produces decisions worth keeping beyond the transcript.
when_not_to_use: Give the project a home for durable decisions first, or the skill has nowhere to write.
notes: The extending page calls this playbook /grill-and-record while the cookbook documents it as /grill-with-docs. Run /help to see the name your build exposes.

name: /taste
description: Apply a flat checklist of visual defaults to avoid, so generated frontend UI stops looking machine-made.

examples.command: /taste Build the landing page from the README
examples.explanation: Generate UI with the anti-slop checklist applied.

when_to_use: You are generating a UI and want to avoid the purple gradient, centered hero, three-card grid look.
when_not_to_use: It never prescribes a specific look; an explicit request from you overrides the checklist.

name: .agents/skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md
description: A skill committed to a repository, shared with anyone who clones it.

examples.explanation: Author a project skill the whole team gets on clone.
Check the skill before committing it.

when_to_use: Package a repeatable workflow the agent should load on demand in this repository.
when_not_to_use: Project skills load only after you trust the workspace.
notes: Muse Code also scans repo-local .codex/skills and .claude/skills, and user skills in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/muse/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.claude/skills, and $CODEX_HOME/skills.
